value.body: An actuarial analyst uses statistics and financial mathematics to estimate risk and to price insurance policies and pension plans. Employers include life and general insurers, reinsurers, consulting firms and analytics centres. A typical day involves cleaning policy and claims data, running models in Excel or R, and checking reserve and pricing calculations.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc Mathematics/Statistics, B.Com or B.Tech, plus actuarial exams

items.label: Professional body
items.note: Entry to its exams is through the ACET test

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Clearing the ACET and a few IAI papers before graduating improves the chance of an analyst or trainee role at an insurer or consulting firm. Many freshers keep writing exams while working; employers often support exam fees and study leave.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: R, Python or SQL for data work
Writing clear summaries of model results

value.title: At a glance
items: Full qualification as a Fellow usually takes several years of exams alongside work.
Typical next steps: actuarial associate, then fellow in pricing, reserving or pensions.
Exam pass rates are low, so progress is often slower than planned.
